Institut Maupertuis is a research and technology transfer organization based in France. It focuses on advanced manufacturing technologies, working closely with industry partners to develop and implement innovative solutions. Here are some key points about the institute.
Overview
Location: Based in Rennes, Brittany, France.
Founded: Established in 2003.
Mission: To facilitate the transfer of innovative technologies from research to industry, focusing on enhancing manufacturing processes.
Core Activities
Research and Development: The institute conducts applied research in collaboration with universities, research centers, and industrial partners.Technology 
Transfer: It helps industries adopt cutting-edge technologies, improving efficiency and productivity.
Training and Education: The institute provides training programs and workshops to equip professionals with the latest technological skills.
Areas of Expertise
Additive Manufacturing: Working on 3D printing technologies and materials to create complex and high-performance parts, as: 
 - Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM), controlled atmosphere;
 - Wire Laser Additive Manufacturing (WLAM), controlled atmosphere;
Materials: Titanium (TA6V, Ti40), Inconel (718 & 625), Stainless steel, Steel, Aluminium, Copper, Bronze and all wire from D0.5mm to D3.2mm.
Laser welding: Laser welding, Arc Welding, Hybrid welding (Laser + Arc).
Friction Stir Welding: Assembly without melting pool (All aluminium series, Copper, Bronze).
Metrology and Quality Control: Implementing advanced techniques for precise measurement and quality assurance in manufacturing processes.
Digital Manufacturing: Leveraging digital technologies, including simulation and digital twins, to optimize manufacturing operations. 
Software: Path planning software, monitoring software. 
Robotics: Developing and integrating robotic systems for various industrial applications.
Collaborations
Institut Maupertuis collaborates with numerous academic and industrial partners, including:
Universities: Engaging in joint research projects with academic institutions.
Industries: Partnering with companies from various sectors, such as aerospace, automotive, and healthcare, to address specific technological challenges.
Impact
The institute plays a crucial role in advancing manufacturing technologies in France and Europe, contributing to the competitiveness of the industrial sector. It is recognized for its expertise in bridging the gap between research and practical industrial applications.

The NTT Group, operating globally under the unified brand NTT, Inc. since July 1, 2025, is one of the world’s leading technology and telecommunications groups. In 2025, NTT implemented a global corporate identity renewal to consolidate its diverse technology, telecommunications and infrastructure businesses under one unified global brand. The Group maintains extensive global operations across telecommunications, digital infrastructure, cloud platforms, cybersecurity and advanced technology research.

NTT DATA serves as the global technology, digital infrastructure and innovation powerhouse of the NTT Group. It is the only company worldwide that owns and operates the full digital value chain from subsea cables to satellites. This includes more than 150,000 kilometers of subsea fiber cables supported by its own marine vessels, a global data center platform with more than 155 data centers in over 20 countries and more than six million square feet of capacity, one of the world’s largest IP backbones, the fourth largest private 5G provider, and satellite-based IoT infrastructure. NTT DATA’s infrastructure is designed to support global digitalization at scale.

The company manages 300 billion USD in assets with zero debt, employs more than 190,000 people in over 70 countries and invests 3.6 billion USD annually in research and development. It has more than 17,000 data and AI practitioners and over 100,000 employees certified in generative AI. NTT DATA is ranked number two globally in application and infrastructure services by Gartner, recognized as an emerging leader in generative AI consulting and implementation and ranked number three globally in managed services by IDC. Its global partnerships include NVIDIA, Cisco, HPE and Dell.

NTT Germany AG & Co. KG is one of the German entities within the NTT ecosystem and an integral part of NTT DATA’s European presence. The company is headquartered in Bad Homburg and delivers advanced IT and digital transformation services to private and public-sector clients in Germany. Its services include enterprise connectivity solutions such as internet, fiber and wireless networking, cloud and data center services, managed IT and cybersecurity operations, data and AI-driven digital transformation and consulting and integration services for numerous technology solutions and vendors.

NTT Germany employs approximately 1,100 professionals and is fully integrated into NTT DATA’s global workforce of more than 190,000 employees. By leveraging NTT DATA’s global infrastructure, research capabilities and technical expertise, NTT Germany provides secure, scalable and future-ready technology solutions across Germany’s enterprise and public‑sector landscape.

entityDescription:
QKZ is a deeptech venture focused on enabling quantum safe communications for the next generation of connectivity, especially in hybrid terrestrial and non terrestrial networks, including NTN. We believe the future internet will be built across multiple layers of infrastructure such as fiber, 5G, private networks, satellite links, and emerging NTN architectures. Trust and security must work seamlessly across all of them.
Mission: Make quantum safe security deployable and operational in real networks. We reduce the barrier to adopting quantum resistant security by turning complex cryptographic capabilities, including QKD, PQC, and classical mechanisms, into infrastructure grade building blocks that network operators and critical organizations can use without bespoke engineering.
Vision: Become the system layer that makes quantum safe connectivity a standard feature of global networks. As NTN expands coverage to remote areas, maritime, aviation, and space ground links, the security model must evolve beyond best effort encryption toward measurable, auditable, and resilient security. Our long term vision is a world where secure connectivity is not limited by geography or dependence on third party infrastructure, and where cryptographic strength can adapt over time as threats and regulations change.
Technical vision: We focus on system level crypto agility for heterogeneous networks. Networks will increasingly combine classical transport paths with intermittent or variable quality links, including satellite and NTN. This requires security mechanisms that can dynamically adapt to changing link conditions and risk profiles. Our technical direction is hybrid orchestration of QKD and PQC, where quantum key material can be used when available, and robust PQC based mechanisms maintain continuity when quantum links are degraded or unavailable. The key challenge is not inventing new algorithms, but making security choices operational through policy driven selection, controlled fallback, lifecycle management, and auditability of decisions.
From a networking perspective, NTN introduces unique constraints such as latency variability, intermittent connectivity, diverse trust boundaries, and complex supply chains. These constraints amplify the need for transparent and resilient security controls. QKZ emphasizes end to end policies, survivable degradation strategies, and evidence based security, including logs and audit trails that explain which cryptographic posture was active at a given time and why.
In summary, QKZ bridges the gap between quantum security research and deployable, resilient security for global connectivity. We build foundations for quantum safe networking that can scale from terrestrial infrastructure to NTN enabled architectures, ensuring that future networks are both globally reachable and trustworthy.
